title: Machine learning prioritizes compounds active against heterogeneous glioblastoma stem-cell models
summary: Researchers trained cell-survival predictors on image-based screening data from six patient-derived glioblastoma stem-cell lines and screened more than 12,000 compounds. Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.
ai_technology: Machine-learning cell-survival predictors trained on high-throughput phenotypic screening
organization: University of Edinburgh and Cancer Research UK Scotland Centre

evidence.tested: Experimental follow-up identified three compounds with activity across the GBM phenotype; HSP90 inhibitor XL-888 eliminated all six tested lines at nanomolar IC50 values, with analyses consistent with HSP90 inhibition and downstream client-protein disruption.
evidence.unknown: This is an in-vitro lead-discovery study across six patient-derived cell lines, not clinical efficacy. XL-888 is an existing HSP90 inhibitor and its proposed development as a GBM lead needs medicinal-chemistry optimization, including improved blood–brain-barrier penetration; no patient outcomes are reported.
evidence.ai_role: ML models trained on in-house imaging/compound-response data predicted cell survival and prioritized compounds from a >12,000-compound screen; experimental assays across patient-derived GBM stem-cell models validated three leads and tested mechanisms. Researchers performed the wet-lab work and mechanism analyses.
